questions.prompt: "Being at least 16 years old is NECESSARY for getting a driving permit in this town." Which conditional says the same thing?

choices.text: If a person has a driving permit, then the person is at least 16.
If a person is at least 16, then the person has a driving permit.
If a person is under 16, then the person may still get a permit.
A person is at least 16 and has a permit.

questions.correct_answer: If a person has a driving permit, then the person is at least 16.

questions.prompt: "You may enter the museum only if you have a ticket." Which statement means the same?

choices.text: If you have a ticket, then you may enter the museum.
You have a ticket and you enter.
If you have no ticket, then you may still enter.
If you enter the museum, then you have a ticket.

questions.correct_answer: If you enter the museum, then you have a ticket.

questions.prompt: In logic, "P unless Q" means "if not Q, then P". Which statement means the same as "The picnic is held unless it rains"?

choices.text: If it rains, the picnic is held.
If it does not rain, the picnic is held.
If the picnic is held, it does not rain.
If it does not rain, the picnic is not held.

questions.correct_answer: If it does not rain, the picnic is held.

questions.prompt: Being a square is a NECESSARY condition for being a rectangle.
n is a whole number. Which condition is NECESSARY for "n is divisible by 6"?

sections.relationship: Necessary and sufficient conditions are both stated as conditionals. A student must first rewrite everyday sentences in if-then form.
sections.author_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions are both stated as conditionals. A student must first rewrite everyday sentences in if-then form.

questions.prompt: Rewrite "All birds have feathers" as a conditional.

choices.text: If an animal is a bird, then it has feathers.
If an animal is not a bird, then it has no feathers.
If an animal has feathers, then it is a bird.

questions.correct_answer: If an animal is a bird, then it has feathers.

questions.prompt: Rewrite "When the bell rings, class ends" as a conditional.

choices.text: If class ends, then the bell rings.
The bell rings and class ends.
If the bell does not ring, class does not end.
If the bell rings, then class ends.

questions.correct_answer: If the bell rings, then class ends.

What is the conclusion of "If a number ends in 5, it is divisible by 5"?

sections.skill: Necessary means required; sufficient means enough
sections.relationship: Students who mix up "required" and "enough" reverse every translation. Everyday examples fix the meaning.
sections.author_note: Students who mix up "required" and "enough" reverse every translation. Everyday examples fix the meaning.

questions.prompt: A concert lets in only people who hold a ticket. Holding a ticket is NECESSARY for getting in.
Having fuel is sufficient for a gas car to run.
Which is SUFFICIENT for a whole number to be even?
If A is sufficient for B, then whenever B happens, A happens.
Being a mammal is ___ for being a dog.

sections.relationship: Harder: conditions that are necessary but not sufficient, and the reverse.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: "n is even" is necessary for "n is divisible by 6". Give a whole number n that shows it is NOT sufficient: n is even but not divisible by 6.
questions.rule: (isEven(n) and n % 6 != 0 and isInteger(n)) and isInteger(n) and n >= 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (isEven(n) and n % 6 != 0 and isInteger(n)) and isInteger(n) and n >= 0 (example: n = 4)

questions.prompt: n is a whole number. Which condition is SUFFICIENT for "n is divisible by 4"?

choices.text: n is divisible by 2 and by 3

questions.prompt: "A triangle is equilateral only if it is isosceles (has at least two equal sides)." Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Being equilateral is necessary for being isosceles.
Being isosceles is sufficient for being equilateral.
Being isosceles is necessary for being equilateral.
The two conditions mean the same thing.

questions.correct_answer: Being isosceles is necessary for being equilateral.

questions.prompt: "You get the discount unless you pay late." Using "P unless Q" = "if not Q, then P", which person is guaranteed the discount?

choices.text: someone who did not pay late

questions.correct_answer: someone who did not pay late

sections.relationship: Expert: combine several necessary and sufficient conditions.

questions.prompt: Facts: A is sufficient for B. B is sufficient for C. Which statement must be true?
For whole numbers n from 1 to 60, condition X: "n is divisible by 4"; condition Y: "n is divisible by 6". How many n satisfy Y but not X (showing X is not necessary for Y)?
Which condition on a whole number n is BOTH necessary and sufficient for "n is divisible by 10"?

choices.text: n is divisible by 2 and by 5

questions.correct_answer: n is divisible by 2 and by 5

questions.prompt: If A is necessary for B and B is necessary for A, then A and B are always both true or both false.
Give a whole number n for which "n is a multiple of 3" holds but "n is a multiple of 9" fails, showing that being a multiple of 3 is not sufficient for being a multiple of 9.
questions.rule: (n % 3 == 0 and n % 9 != 0 and isInteger(n)) and isInteger(n) and n >= 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (n % 3 == 0 and n % 9 != 0 and isInteger(n)) and isInteger(n) and n >= 0 (example: n = 6)
